scope: The Political MAYHEM site as a whole: MAYHEM architecture, sport-legibility translations, evidence states, lifecycle states, tipping controls, audit language, analytical constructs and public-interface terminology. Native political terminology belongs in the separate Political Master Glossary.
rules: Preserve canonical site terms and internal codes for audit integrity.
Translate internal MAYHEM language into ordinary public language.
Do not contaminate the Political Master Glossary with MAYHEM/site architecture.
Sport labels are interface mappings and never override canonical political entities or evidence semantics.
A missed pre-outcome checkpoint may be captured late only while the target remains open; preserve both due time and actual capture time.
Never backdate a late capture or use post-outcome information to reconstruct a pre-outcome checkpoint.
Retrospective evidence discovery and ongoing capture are both valid evidence streams; preserve source/event time and MAYHEM discovery/capture time separately.
Later-discovered evidence may explain or audit an earlier frozen prediction but must never be credited to that prediction's original evidentiary lineage.

terms.plain_language: The public MAYHEM view of continuous evidence capture, target-specific checkpoints, freezes, outcomes and audits.
terms.research_use: Control timed evidence capture and expose completed, late or missed checkpoints.

terms.plain_language: A probability-forecast accuracy measure used to test how well frozen probabilities perform over time.
terms.research_use: Audit calibration of genuine contemporaneous tips.

terms.plain_language: The recorded time at which evidence was actually acquired.
terms.research_use: Test contemporaneity and information timing.

terms.plain_language: A checkpoint captured after its scheduled time but while the relevant tipping target was still open.
terms.research_use: Preserve useful forward evidence without pretending it was captured on time.

terms.plain_language: A scheduled or event-triggered evidence-capture stage in the MAYHEM workflow.
terms.research_use: Structure repeated research and audit actions.

terms.plain_language: The probability or confidence attached to a genuine MAYHEM tip at a specific evidence cutoff.
terms.research_use: Compare later with outcomes and calibration.

terms.plain_language: The always-active political environment within which teams, players, signals and tipping targets change over time.
terms.research_use: Prevent the system from treating politics as idle between elections.

terms.plain_language: Evidence-state label meaning a claim conflicts with stronger or newer verified evidence.
terms.research_use: Trigger contradiction resolution instead of silent replacement.

terms.plain_language: A MAYHEM comparison between a current state and a longer baseline.
terms.research_use: Detect material change in party, actor or field state.

terms.plain_language: A test of whether an existing tip remains supported after new evidence arrives.
terms.research_use: Detect stale or inertial selections.

terms.plain_language: The risk that apparently separate observations derive from the same underlying source or mechanism.
terms.research_use: Prevent correlated evidence from being counted as independent support.

terms.plain_language: The traceable chain connecting a conclusion or tip to observations and original sources.
terms.research_use: Audit provenance and source independence.

terms.plain_language: A mandatory review triggered when a genuine frozen MAYHEM tip is wrong or materially incomplete. The original decision is judged against evidence available by its freeze, while later-discovered evidence may be used to explain missed mechanisms or causation if its timing is preserved.
terms.research_use: Separate evaluation of the original pre-freeze decision from later explanatory learning without rewriting the frozen prediction.

terms.plain_language: Public sports-language shorthand for a defined political outcome-bearing tipping target.
terms.research_use: Make discrete political targets legible without changing their canonical political meaning.

terms.plain_language: Evidence-supported change in a party or actor state over time.
terms.research_use: Translate longitudinal political state into familiar sports language.

terms.plain_language: The last valid pre-outcome tip state for a defined target.
terms.research_use: Lock the decision boundary against hindsight.

terms.plain_language: The preserved MAYHEM selection and probability that cannot be rewritten after the relevant outcome.
terms.research_use: Anchor later grading and failure review to the genuine prior position.

terms.plain_language: The MAYHEM test of whether combining public information produced a decision-relevant edge beyond any individual source.
terms.research_use: Assess timing, fragmentation, aggregation and information absorption.

terms.plain_language: A sports-style comparative ordering of political teams using a named evidence-derived metric.
terms.research_use: Expose comparative form while keeping the underlying metric explicit.

terms.plain_language: The public selected outcome for a defined, auditable political target.
terms.research_use: Expose the current selection while preserving its cutoff and lineage.

terms.plain_language: A scheduled checkpoint whose target time passed without capture; it is never reconstructed after the target has closed.
terms.research_use: Preserve timing failures as audit evidence.

terms.plain_language: Lifecycle state meaning an event has resolved in practice but an authoritative outcome has not yet been persisted.
terms.research_use: Trigger result acquisition and reconciliation.

terms.plain_language: Public sports-language label for a political actor.
terms.research_use: Make actor-level intelligence legible while canonical data retains political actor IDs and roles.

terms.plain_language: Persistent MAYHEM record combining actor identity, role, observations, signals, contradictions and source lineage.
terms.research_use: Accumulate actor intelligence longitudinally.

terms.plain_language: The longitudinal political period within which teams, players, targets and outcomes accumulate.
terms.research_use: Provide a season-like public frame for continuous political state.

terms.plain_language: MAYHEM architecture for comparing baselines, deltas, pressure events and outcome validation across domains.
terms.research_use: Transfer continuity-analysis structure into political intelligence.

terms.plain_language: A material disruption used to test whether a prior political or analytical state remains stable.
terms.research_use: Research before-and-after evidence around leadership, candidacy, institutional, polling or policy shocks.

terms.plain_language: Internal state meaning a mandatory evidence, contradiction, calibration or audit gate remains unresolved.
terms.research_use: Direct research toward the unresolved condition.

terms.plain_language: A continuity measure tracking persistence of named political actors, roles and affiliations within a team.
terms.research_use: Compare current and prior party-team states.

terms.plain_language: The risk that an existing tip is retained because it is already established rather than because current evidence still supports it.
terms.research_use: Trigger falsification and opposing-case research.

terms.plain_language: A potentially relevant observation that has not yet reached verified-fact status.
terms.research_use: Require corroboration, contradiction testing or explicit exclusion.

terms.plain_language: One bounded, provenance-linked observation tracked separately for later relationship to political state and outcomes.
terms.research_use: Prevent bundled narratives from hiding which observation actually mattered.

terms.plain_language: The MAYHEM classification of the type of source behind an observation.
terms.research_use: Guide source priority and later performance auditing.

terms.plain_language: A longitudinal evidence-supported assessment of how consistently a source performs for a defined use.
terms.research_use: Use only after accumulated audit evidence.

terms.plain_language: The longer-run reference state used to compare current political conditions and deltas.
terms.research_use: Anchor later continuity and form analysis.

terms.plain_language: Public sports-language label for a political party.
terms.research_use: Make party competition legible while canonical data retains actual party identities.

terms.plain_language: The preservation of both when a political fact or event occurred and when MAYHEM discovered or captured the evidence for it.
terms.research_use: Allow retrospective discovery and ongoing capture to coexist while preventing later evidence from being falsely credited to an earlier frozen prediction.

terms.plain_language: The outcome label showing whether a genuine frozen MAYHEM tip was correct, incorrect, partial or void.
terms.research_use: Keep ordinary tipping result separate from deeper calibration analysis.

terms.plain_language: A defined political outcome that can be timestamped, versioned, frozen and later verified.
terms.research_use: Separate auditable discrete predictions from the continuously live political field.

terms.plain_language: Explicit recognition that available evidence does not support a stronger directional claim.
terms.research_use: Prevent incomplete evidence from becoming false certainty.

terms.plain_language: Evidence state meaning a specific factual claim is supported by sufficient source material.
terms.research_use: Preserve evidence classification and source lineage.

terms.plain_language: The authoritative political result against which a frozen MAYHEM tip is graded.
terms.research_use: Close the target lifecycle without hindsight rewriting.
